change_interpretations.engineering_summary: The pedal demand threshold for triggering the torque response was raised from 70 % to 90 %; the 100 ms response time limit remains unchanged, meaning the requirement now applies only to higher pedal demands.

assessments.reason: The test steps the pedal to 75 % demand, which is below the new 90 % threshold, so it does not exercise the changed condition.
The test uses an 85 % pedal demand, still below the new 90 % threshold, and does not record response timing, so it may no longer verify VCU-DR-01.
assessments.recommended_action: Discuss with test owner whether to adjust the pedal demand to >90 % or separate the arbitration check.

assessments.reason: The sweep covers 75–95 % demand and records a 92 ms response, which includes the >90 % region required by the revised VCU-DR-01, and the measured time is within the 100 ms limit.
assessments.recommended_action: No change needed; existing PASS evidence satisfies the revised requirement.

assessments.reason: The test validates emergency brake priority only, unrelated to driver torque response threshold.
Validates sensor degradation mode, unrelated to VCU-DR-01.
Checks logging of mode changes, unrelated to torque response timing.
Uses 80 % pedal demand and has no link to VCU-DR-01, so it does not cover the changed condition.
References an unknown legacy requirement and does not involve pedal demand, thus not related to VCU-DR-01.
Compares torque ramp profiles between modes without a timing or demand threshold, not exercising VCU-DR-01.
Injects a 7 ms spike to test signal filtering, unrelated to the torque response demand threshold.
Validates brake override priority, not the driver torque response timing.
Measures ECU wake‑up time, unrelated to VCU-DR-01.
